comments.author: @pallepirat
comments.text: I must admit that I myself am extremely scared by how powerful the models have become and how quickly they are developing. At the moment, there’s a kind of ‘frenzy’, where the main goal is to be the first. There might be political statements about thinking carefully, but so far, no one has hit the brakes. And in relation to how quickly the development will happen, very few people, even those I care about and try to educate, really understand what they are dealing with. Personally, my time horizon for economy and planning is a maximum of 5 years. I often think about how uncertain the future is. On the other hand, I must say that I am lucky. I’m a white man with many degrees and live in a very rich European country. If there’s going to be room for adaptation or societal changes, then we are certainly better positioned than most. But the other day, I spoke with my wife about the people in Africa who generally have a very low level of education. How are they ever going to break out of poverty if education and development come to a halt? That’s another side of the issue that we haven’t even touched yet. As for the new initiative with Worldcoin, I have to admit that I’m skeptical. The idea that 6 million people voting on something makes it democratic, or that the whole world should vote on something, I’m not entirely buying into that. With a European background, I must say that there are significant value differences even among small groups of people. I wouldn’t call it a democratic process. There are also great possibilities for people to be influenced by advertisements or other influences when the numbers are this large. This is of course also true for smaller groups, but I still think there’s a difference.

comments.author: @K.F-R
comments.text:
I have questions.  I fed ChatGPT 4 (with web plugins) these questions and its answers were deeply, deeply worrying (e.g. "I'm sure Worldcoin is taking this very seriously").  Here's a few of the questions.  Maybe your comments section will do better. 
* Biometric data is vulnerable to physical damage and natural wear-and-tear.  Is this scanning age-proof?  Cataract surgery-proof?  What about car accident proof?
* That 10 billion limit.  Is that for real?  Do we inherit ID's because people die.  It's true.  If we inherit ID's we're inheriting relationship and transaction data so it can't be.
* I was under the impression that it was some kind of hashing of the result a proprietary iris scan algorithm.  That seems... weak.  And incompatible with the above.  I'm still confused.
* Why can an artificial iris not be generated and scanned?  The iris-is-complex argument will not cut it - it's just data and if we've learned anything, AI can do stuff we thought was hard.  How long until unique not-humans are a thing?
* That orb, though.  Seriously.  A black box algorithm on a proprietary scanner suite.  They're closed sourcing all this are they?  This can't be right.  That would be a security nightmare - the implicit centralization of information hurts my head.
Surely I need to do more reading.  
I must be missing a lot.  I really hope I'm missing a lot.
I'm hoping ChatGPT did a really crap job of reading the worldcoin site because its summary and understanding did not provide comforting answers.
Right now it feels more like scientology that cryptocurrency.
